title: Constantin von Economo (1876-1931): cytoarchitectonic roots of modern network neuroscience.
abstract: Constantin von Economo (1876-1931) is widely remembered for his seminal description of encephalitis lethargica, yet his broader contribution to cortical organization remains underappreciated. Beyond clinical neurology, von Economo and Georg Koskinas, a neurologist-psychiatrist, contributed to the broader cytoarchitectonic tradition by developing one of the most detailed architectonic frameworks of the human cerebral cortex, emphasizing laminar heterogeneity, regional transition, and structural specialization. These concepts can be reconsidered in relation to contemporary models of large-scale brain organization. In particular, cortical territories associated with von Economo's work, including the anterior insula and anterior cingulate region, are now recognized as key hubs in salience processing and contain the distinctive spindle-shaped neurons later termed von Economo neurons. Recent advances in connectomics, cortical gradient mapping, and laminar neuroimaging have renewed interest in the relationship between cortical microstructure and distributed functional networks. From this perspective, von Economo's work may be viewed not simply as a landmark in classical neuroanatomy, but as a historically important structural framework that can be reinterpreted in relation to modern ideas of structure-function coupling and network-level brain organization. This historical vignette revisits his life, scientific contributions, and enduring relevance to contemporary neuroscience and neurosurgical thinking.

title: Clinical prognosis and neurosurgical management of abusive head trauma: a scoping review.
abstract: This scoping review sought to synthesize the current evidence for prognosis and neurosurgical management in abusive head trauma (AHT), a particularly deadly form of pediatric traumatic brain injury (TBI). Using key search terms such as "abusive head trauma," "neurosurgical procedures," "mortality," and "prognosis," the authors imported articles published between 2009 and 2025 from PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and CINAHL, as well as from citation and gray literature searches of Covidence. Duplicates were removed (n = 3138), and after abstract and full-text screening, 46 articles remained for data extraction. Although these articles addressed more than one category, each was classified according to the primary focus and/or substantive data presented. The included studies examined the relative prognosis of AHT relative to accidental trauma (AT) (n = 10 articles), clinical (n = 16) and demographic (n = 8) prognostic factors in AHT, and neurosurgical management of AHT (n = 12). Compared to AT, AHT was consistently associated with greater mortality, longer and more intensive hospitalizations, as well as higher risks of short- and long-term multisystem dysfunction. Among AHT patients, low admission Glasgow Coma Scale scores, abnormal neuroimaging findings, seizures, retinal hemorrhage, respiratory compromise, and abnormal pupillary reactivity were associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Older age at injury and lower socioeconomic status were also associated with poor outcomes in AHT. Rates of neurosurgical intervention varied widely, with particularly high reoperation rates in those who underwent transfontanelle aspiration for subdural fluid collections. This scoping review highlights the particularly poor prognosis of AHT, underscoring the potential utility of the identified clinical and demographic prognostic factors in guiding closer clinical management or earlier surgical intervention.

title: Patients as Partners: A New Article Type in Anesthesia & Analgesia Extending Perspectives in Practice and Research.
Attention, not scale, drives human-AI alignment in multimodal language prediction.
abstract: Humans routinely draw on visual context to predict upcoming words. To what extent current vision-language models produce comparable behaviour is unclear. Here, we placed five state-of-the-art pretrained systems side-by-side with 600 human participants in a web-based Visual-World Paradigm. On each of 100 six-second movie clips, models and participants received either text-only or synchronised video + text and judged how likely a specified target word was to appear next; human eye movements were tracked throughout. Adding visual context increased model-human alignment in predictability ratings across all architectures (average Δr ≈ 0.18) with no impact of parameter size. When visual context was informative, transformer attention significantly increased alignment. Attention maps from two transformer models corresponded with human gaze, explaining up to 70% of the inter-participant variance when the scene contained informative cues. Notably, cross-modal attention reliably tracked anticipatory human fixations on semantic cues. These results suggest that current transformer-based vision-language models can approximate human behaviour exploiting visual context during language prediction-and that selective attention to informative cues, not sheer model scale, is the principal driver of this alignment.

title: Dual-site multifocal HD-tDCS modulates bilingual language control via brain activity and connectivity.
abstract: Bilinguals rely on language control mechanisms to manage cross-language interference. Interactions between the pre-supplementary motor area (pre-SMA) and the left cerebellum play an important role in bilingual language control. However, our previous brain stimulation study targeting the cerebellum alone failed to detect significant behavioral changes in bilingual language control. In this study, we combined dual-site tDCS with fMRI to investigate its effects on bilingual language control and compared it with conventional single-site tDCS. Using a within-subject design, Chinese-English bilinguals underwent three sessions: pre-stimulation baseline, single-site tDCS over pre-SMA, and dual-site tDCS over pre-SMA and left cerebellum. Following dual-site stimulation, we observed reduced brain activity within the language control network, including the right cerebellar lobule VI, and strengthened thalamo-cerebellar connections during bilingual language production. In a separate behavioral experiment, language switch cost was lower after dual-site stimulation than at baseline but did not differ significantly between dual-site and single-site stimulation. Together, these findings provide preliminary evidence that dual-site tDCS modulates bilingual language control, potentially by strengthening thalamo-cerebellar connectivity and modulating cerebellar neural activity. These results also highlight the functional interaction between the pre-SMA and the cerebellum in supporting bilingual language control.

title: Esketamine alleviates the pain-depression dyad: insights from exploratory transcriptomic profiling and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations within the anterior cingulate cortex.
abstract: The molecular mechanisms driving esketamine (ESK) efficacy in the pain-depression dyad (PDD) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of a sub-anesthetic ESK regimen on cortical expression profiles and exploratory signaling markers within the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into Sham, PDD, and PDD + ESK groups. The PDD model, established via chronic constriction injury (CCI), was validated using a behavioral test battery tracking mechanical allodynia and depression-like phenotypes. On day 21 post-surgery, PDD + ESK rats received a single esketamine injection (15 mg/kg, i.p.). Multi-regional c-Fos expression mapping across the PFC, HPC, and ACC identified the primary responsive structure, followed by dual immunofluorescence for cellular phenotyping. Finally, ACC excitatory neuronal calcium dynamics, exploratory transcriptomic profiles, and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations (including GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation alongside synaptic markers) were evaluated using fiber photometry, RNA sequencing, and Western blotting. ESK alleviated pain hypersensitivity, behavioral despair, and anhedonia in PDD rats. Regional c-Fos profiling identified the ACC as the primary reactive locus, with activation localized predominantly to CaMKIIα-positive neurons. Fiber photometry confirmed that ESK attenuated functional hyperactivation in these ACC excitatory neurons. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling (unadjusted P < 0.05) revealed candidate altered transcripts, identifying Wnt4 as an exploratory molecular marker for further investigation. Subsequent orthogonal protein validations demonstrated that ESK modulated Wnt4 expression alongside concomitant alterations in GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation, parallel with the attenuation of pathologically elevated synaptic protein markers and a restorative trend in synaptic ultrastructure. A single sub-anesthetic ESK dose effectively alleviates PDD behavioral phenotypes in rats. This therapeutic efficacy is associated with Wnt4-related molecular adjustments coupled with putative downstream GSK3β-mTOR signaling alterations within the ACC CaMKIIα-positive neurons, providing exploratory transcriptomic and molecular insights into cortical adaptations in pain-related affective disorders.

title: Thalamic atrophy in active and inactive secondary progressive multiple sclerosis patients: A comparative study.
abstract: Thalamic atrophy may be an indicator of neurodegeneration in people with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (pwSPMS). The atrophy usually begins asymmetrically, and the thalamic asymmetry index (TAI) can be used to estimate the severity of neurodegeneration. SPMS is commonly divided into two groups of active and inactive. No study has compared TAI between SPMS groups and examine its relationships with cognitive and motor measures in pwSPMS. This study aimed to compare the TAI between active and inactive pwSPMS and to examine its relationship with key clinical, cognitive, and motor variables. In this cross-sectional study, 38 pwSPMS (15 active and 23 inactive) were enrolled from February to November 2024. MRI-based volumetric measurements were used to determine thalamic volumes and calculate the TAI. Cognitive and motor tests, including the SDMT, PASAT, and 9HPT were also administered alongside clinical examinations. Active SPMS patients had significantly lower NTV compared to inactive patients (Cohen's d = -1.58, p < 0.001). No significant difference in TAI was observed between groups. NTV correlated with cognitive scores in both active (r = 0.74, P = 0.002) and inactive (r = 0.65, p < 0.001) groups and with disability in the inactive group (r = -0.5, P= 0.014). Active SPMS patients showed worse cognitive and motor performance. Thalamic atrophy is more severe in active SPMS and is associated with worse cognitive and motor outcomes. While thalamic asymmetry did not differentiate between subgroups, it may serve as a marker for functional status in SPMS.

title: Rectal colonization with multidrug-resistant organisms in adult acute leukemia patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a retrospective, longitudinal, single-center study.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract: Rectal colonization with multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) represents a frequent issue in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) for acute leukemia. However, the prognostic significance of MDRO-colonization in these patients remains debated. This retrospective, longitudinal, single-center study included 100 patients with acute myeloid or lymphoblastic leukemia treated at Verona University Hospital from diagnosis to allo-HSCT. MDRO-colonization was monitored by rectal swab at admission and weekly during hospitalization. Colonized patients underwent targeted antibiotic therapy when clinically required. To assess epidemiology, timing, and impact of rectal MDRO-colonization on infection occurrence, infection-related mortality (IRM) within day +100, overall survival (OS), and transplant-related mortality (TRM). Rectal colonization with 44 MDRO strains was detected in 35 (35%) patients undergoing allo-HSCT, either at hospital admission (45.7%) or during hospitalization (54.3%). Enterobacterales accounted for 72.7% of MDROs, with 68.5% of colonizing strains being detected during previous hospital stays for induction or consolidation therapies. MDRO-related bloodstream infections (BSI) occurred in 9 (9%) patients, 7 (77.8%) of whom being rectal carriers. IRM within day +100 was null. OS was significantly lower in MDRO-carriers as compared to non-carriers only at univariate analysis. TRM did not differ significantly between the two groups in both univariate and multivariate analyses. Despite the limitations of a single-center retrospective study, our data show that careful monitoring of rectal colonization and prompt use of targeted antibiotics may temper the negative impact of MDRO-related infections in adult acute leukemia patients undergoing allo-HSCT, even in the setting of a higher rate of BSIs.

title: Intranasal delivery of regenerative biologics for neurological disorders: a systematic review of clinical studies.
abstract: Intranasal delivery is a minimally invasive route for administering regenerative biologics to the central nervous system while bypassing the blood-brain barrier. Human clinical evidence for this approach across neurological disorders remains dispersed across multiple disease areas, biologic classes, dosing frameworks, and delivery methods, limiting field-level synthesis. This study was conducted to systematically evaluate the safety, dosing characteristics, delivery method heterogeneity, and disease-specific direction of effect of intranasal regenerative biologics, including mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), neural stem cells (NSCs), exosomes, secretome and conditioned medium, breast milk-derived biologic preparations, and related regenerative products, in patients with neurological disorders. An International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO)-registered systematic review was conducted and reported in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines, with synthesis performed in accordance with Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) recommendations. PubMed, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ChiCTR were searched from January 2015 to August 2026. Risk of Bias (RoB) was assessed using study design-appropriate validated tools, including Cochrane RoB 2 and Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) and methodological quality of uncontrolled studies was appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklists for Case Series and Case Reports. Sixteen publications comprising 18 patient cohorts across 12 neurological conditions were included. No treatment-related serious adverse events were reported. Most cohorts showed clinical improvement, while one reported stabilization, though the predominantly uncontrolled designs mean placebo response and natural disease history cannot be ruled out. However, the biologic class was strongly confounded by disease indication, dosing was heterogeneous and non-comparable, and five delivery techniques were used. By integrating clinical evidence across biologic classes and neurological disorders, this review defines the current safety landscape, highlights major methodological gaps, and provides a framework for standardized future intranasal regenerative trials. Adequately powered, standardized, and controlled trials are required before clinical adoption can be considered.

title: A solitary brain metastasis from gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma 13 years after curative multimodality treatment: a case report and review of the literature.
abstract: Brain metastases in gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma are uncommon and can cause substantial neurological morbidity. Here, we report the case of a 58-year-old patient who developed a solitary brain metastasis thirteen years after curative-intent multimodality treatment for a Siewert type II gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GEJA). The intracranial lesion was initially radiologically suspected to be a primary brain tumour, while systemic restaging showed no extracranial disease. Histopathology, immunohistochemistry, clinical history, and methylome profiling supported metastatic recurrence from the prior GEJA. This case is noteworthy for the exceptionally long disease-free interval, the brain-only presentation after routine oncological surveillance had ended, and the diagnostic importance of tissue confirmation and integrated pathological assessment when a new intracranial lesion appears many years after curative treatment. This case supports maintaining late metastatic recurrence in the differential diagnosis of symptomatic brain lesions without implying a role for routine neuroimaging in asymptomatic long-term survivors.

title: A non-randomized trial of the effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on cognitive performance and resting state connectivity.
abstract: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has shown promise for enhancing cognition and emotion regulation. To date, most human studies have focused on narrow learning paradigms that limit our understanding of how taVNS influences complex, integrative cognitive operations. Moreover, the underlying mechanisms of taVNS are still not well understood. Building on preclinical findings that vagus nerve stimulation enhances cognitive flexibility and memory in animal models, this study investigated whether acute taVNS can modulate executive function and neural connectivity in healthy adults. Using a quasi-experimental design, forty healthy participants received either active or sham taVNS while completing executive function tasks and adaptive cognitive training (BrainHQ). High-density electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded during stimulation to assess cortical activity and functional connectivity across frequency bands. Multivariate analyses demonstrated significant effects of taVNS on cognitive function and EEG. Post-hoc group comparisons showed that compared to sham stimulation, active taVNS was associated with improved BrainHQ performance and decreased delta-band connectivity in left frontal, central, and parietal regions. Delta-band connectivity during active taVNS was positively associated with pre-to-post improvements in mood. No difference in executive function tasks was found between active and sham taVNS. Sensitivity analyses using adjusted models showed that these effects were sensitive to age, sex, and education. By evaluating multiple dimensions of executive function, these exploratory findings suggest that active taVNS may influence selected aspects of executive performance and frontal-parietal delta connectivity, potentially reflecting enhanced neural efficiency arising from the interaction between vagally mediated neuromodulation and continuously adaptive cognitive demands. However, these effects did not survive multiple-comparison correction and should therefore be interpreted cautiously and replicated in larger, prospectively powered studies.

title: Resilience and clinical recovery in first-episode schizophrenia: a 10-year longitudinal study of clinically recovered, non-recovered, and healthy control participants.
abstract: Research on resilience in clinical recovery following first-episode schizophrenia (FES) remains limited, and few longitudinal studies achieve sufficient retention to capture long-term trajectories. To address this, the Oslo Schizophrenia Recovery Study (OSR) was designed to examine resilience over time in FES. Investigating resilience is essential for understanding how individuals exposed to schizophrenia may achieve favorable outcomes. We addressed two primary questions: First, how does resilience change over time in individuals with FES compared with healthy controls. Second, whether longitudinal resilience trajectories within the FES group differ between participants who meet predefined clinical recovery criteria compared to those who do not. Repeated assessments were conducted across 12 clinical evaluations. The sample comprised 28 individuals with FES and 28 healthy controls. Resilience was measured with the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and social and role functioning were indexed using the Global Functioning Scales. The data were analyzed using linear multilevel models. Candidate longitudinal mixed-effects models were compared using the small-sample corrected Akaike Information Criterion (AICc), with parameters estimated by maximum likelihood. At 10-year follow-up, retention was 79%. Half of the FES group achieved clinical recovery. Model estimates indicated increasing resilience over time in the FES group, whereas resilience in healthy controls remained relatively stable, although statistical support for differential trajectories between groups was limited. Clinically recovered individuals showed a steeper increase in resilience. In contrast, non-recovered individuals exhibited only modest, gradual improvements, with resilience levels remaining lower at study completion. Different resilience trajectories were observed between clinically recovered and non-recovered individuals with FES, with greater improvements in resilience associated with recovery. Although causality remains uncertain and differences to healthy controls were less robust, these findings highlight the value of repeated longitudinal assessments of resilience in FES, both to more precisely characterize resilience trajectories and to reduce drop-out rates.

title: Targeting TLR4 alleviates the progression of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by regulating central resident cells and Th1/Th17 cell differentiation.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease characterized by neuroinflammation. Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) is a receptor for damage-associated molecular patterns, such as high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) and plays a role in innate immunity. However, its precise role and cellular dynamics in MS pathogenesis are unclear. Using the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model, we mapped the expression dynamics of TLR4 and found that in the spinal cords, the cell type associated with the disease shifted from neurons to activated glia. To establish causality, we subjected TLR4 -/- mice to EAE and observed significantly attenuated disease severity, reduced demyelination, and preserved neuronal integrity, alongside suppressed microglial and astrocytic activation. Furthermore, TLR4 deficiency was not merely dampening CNS-localized inflammation but was also associated with suppressed peripheral MOG35-55-specific Th1/Th17 effector responses, as evidenced by reduced production of IFN-γ and IL-17A in lymphoid organs, together with reduced TNF-α, as well as diminished expression of the Th1/Th17 lineage-defining transcription factors T-bet and RORγt in the spinal cord infiltrates. This suggests that TLR4 plays a key role in EAE pathology by connecting peripheral Th1/Th17 differentiation with central glial inflammatory responses. Critically, to translate these findings, we evaluated the small-molecule TLR4 antagonist TAK-242. While prophylactic administration was effective, therapeutic dosing initiated after disease onset still significantly alleviated clinical scores and delayed progression, highlighting its potential for clinical intervention. Overall, our results demonstrate that targeting TLR4 simultaneously curtails pathogenic T-cell differentiation and local neuroinflammation, establishing TLR4 as a dual-action therapeutic target for MS.

title: A guide to selecting high-performing antibodies for ASM (UniProt ID: P17405) for use in western blot and immunoprecipitation.
abstract: The SMPD1 gene encodes the acid sphingomyelinase (ASM) protein, a lysosomal enzyme essential for hydrolysing sphingomyelin into ceramide and phosphorylcholine, a key step in lipid metabolism and membrane homeostasis. Here we have characterized nine ASM commercial antibodies for western blot and immunoprecipitation using a standardized experimental protocol based on comparing read-outs in knockout cell lines and isogenic parental controls. These studies are part of a larger, collaborative initiative seeking to address antibody reproducibility issues by characterizing commercially available antibodies for human proteins and publishing the results openly as a resource for the scientific community. While the use of antibodies and protocols vary between laboratories, we encourage readers to use this report as a guide to select the most appropriate antibodies for their specific needs.

title: Unraveling the Relationship Between Nr4a2 and Fezf1 Expression in the Developing Feline Telencephalon Within the Genoarchitectonic Context of Claustral and Amygdalar Development.
abstract: The developmental origin and molecular specification of the lateral pallium remain incompletely understood, particularly with respect to the emergence of the claustrum and its relationship to neighboring pallial territories. Here, we provide a developmental and genoarchitectonic analysis of the feline lateral pallium and its derivatives, focusing on the expression of Nr4a2 and Fezf1. Our results demonstrate that the lateral pallium acquires a distinct molecular identity before the onset of Nr4a2 expression. Beginning at E26/27, a Satb2-positive and Fezf2-low domain can be identified below the ventral rim of the cortical plate, preceding the appearance of a restricted Nr4a2-positive claustral focus that subsequently expands to encompass both claustral and endopiriform populations, indicating that Nr4a2 is a marker of claustral differentiation rather than of lateropallial identity. The spatial organization of the developing claustral complex resembles that described in rodents and is consistent with the cortical ring theory. In contrast to the restricted developmental profile of Nr4a2, Fezf1 exhibited a broad and dynamic expression pattern. Early Fezf1 expression was widely distributed among pallial progenitor populations, suggesting a role in neurogenesis rather than in regional specification, whereas later expression became restricted to selected populations of the piriform cortex and the amygdala. Comparisons with Otp and Sim1 expression further suggest contributions from both telencephalic and hypothalamic sources to Fezf1-positive amygdalar populations. Our findings do not support a specific association between Fezf1 expression and the lateropallial mantle; instead, Fezf1 appears to participate in pallial neurogenesis and amygdalar differentiation. Collectively, our findings refine the current understanding of feline lateropallial development, clarify the significance of Nr4a2 and Fezf1 expression, and provide a comparative framework for interpreting claustral and amygdalar regionalization across mammals.
keywords: Nuclear Receptor Subfamily 4, Group A, Member 2

title: Maximum Gape in Developing Macaca mulatta.
abstract: Maximum gape and bite force are two key metrics of primate craniodental performance, but without mitigating adaptations, large gapes are associated with reduced bite force. Primate craniodental morphology undergoes functional transitions across development, but how these performance variables vary with life-history transitions is unknown. Maximum gapes of 211 rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) spanning infancy to post-prime developmental stages from Cayo Santiago (Puerto Rico) were collected in vivo, and jaw leverage, a contributor to bite force, was calculated from skeletal measurements of the same individuals post-mortem. Allometric relationships were tested using a combination of OLS regressions and mixed-effects models with developmental stage and sex as interaction terms. In vivo gape did not differ from isometry relative to body mass and jaw length across developmental stages by sex, but jaw leverage was significantly lower in larger compared to smaller macaques. The largest developmental differences occurred between pre-prime and prime individuals. Canine length scaled with positive allometry against body mass and jaw length in males but not females, while maximum gape scaled with negative allometry relative to canine length in both sexes. These results indicate that macaques undergo a functional tradeoff between jaw leverage and gape around the onset of sexual dimorphism. Pre-prime macaques exhibit relatively greater jaw leverage, whereas adults maintain proportionate gape relative to body and jaw size at reduced mechanical advantage. The eruption of large canines in males does not influence linear gape outside of size differences captured by body mass and jaw length.

title: Circuit Topology Shapes the Mapping Between Excitatory-Inhibitory Input Composition and Aperiodic Spectral Slope.
abstract: Aperiodic ([Formula: see text]) spectral components are widely interpreted as markers of excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance, but this interpretation spans levels from synaptic currents and microcircuit spiking to population field potentials. Whether macroscopic spectral slope can index microcircuit-level E/I input independently of circuit architecture remains unresolved. This study introduces a connectome- and morphology-constrained framework that embeds electron-microscopy-reconstructed cortical microcircuits in near-critical propagation dynamics and generates field potentials under fixed synaptic, membrane, and forward-modeling parameters. By linking controlled synaptic E/I input, microcircuit spiking propagation, and macroscopic spectra, the framework directly tests the explanatory level of the aperiodic exponent. Across matched E/I regimes, the strength of the E/I input-[Formula: see text] relationship differed between biological and topology-randomized networks, yielding a significant E/I input × topology interaction. To test whether this architecture-dependent mapping extends to biological systems, paired cortical ECoG and thalamic EThG recordings from juvenile pigs were analyzed. Under the same systemic propofol perturbation, exponent changes were stronger in thalamus than cortex and remained so after accounting for global state shifts, baseline spectra, and distance from criticality. These findings identify circuit architecture as a determinant of how microcircuit E/I input is transformed into macroscopic aperiodic spectra, defining the level-specific interpretability of spectral slope.

title: Guiding principles for modelling cellular transport homeostasis.
abstract: Cellular transport homeostasis evolved as a universal strategy linking the dynamic interactions between membrane transport, metabolism and biosynthesis in all cells. The entangled nature of these interactions, together with the effects from additional processes influencing homeostatic variables generate complexities that render intuition an unreliable interpreter and predictor of cell responses often prompting for modelling help. The main variables in transport homeostasis are membrane potentials, cell volume, ion and neutral solute fluxes through active and passive membrane transporters, cytoplasmic amounts and concentrations of soluble ions and neutral solutes, charge and concentrations of impermeant cytoplasmic solutes, charge and osmotic coefficient of cytoplasmic proteins, and cytoplasmic H+, Ca2+ and Mg2+ buffering. Models of cellular transport homeostasis developed to explain puzzling, unexpected or conflicting observations in epithelia, red blood cells, malaria-infected red blood cells, reticulocytes, sickle cells, and plant guard cells proved essential for explaining underlying mechanisms in many experimental, physiological and pathological contexts and for elucidating conflicts greatly expanding our knowledge of the cell systems investigated thus far. The transport homeostasis loop is an ancient circuit that preserves cellular integrity. In this cycle, metabolic ATP powers families of membrane pumps that sustain ionic gradients across plasma membranes. These gradients act as secondary sources of energy for the passive transport of ions through channels and through ion-coupled solute carriers. These, in turn, supply the substrates for metabolic ATP production and for the biosynthesis of proteins, lipids, RNA and DNA that replace decayed membrane transporters, closing the transport homeostasis loop. This review outlines the foundational principles applied when developing models of this dynamic circuit and of the achievements resulting from their application in different cell types.

title: Effect of Blonanserin on Neurotrophic Factors in Patients With Non-Responsive First-Episode Schizophrenia Treated With Early Risperidone Monotherapy-A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: International journal of methods in psychiatric research
abstract: To investigate the efficacy of Blonanserin in patients with schizophrenia who were refractory to Risperidone monotherapy and its effects on various neurotrophic factors. A total of 120 patients with first-episode schizophrenia who were hospitalized in our hospital from January 2022 to December 2023 and did not respond to early Risperidone monotherapy were selected as the study participants. They were randomly divided into a control group and a research group, with 60 cases in each group. The control group was treated with Clozapine, and the research group was treated with Blonanserin for 3 months. The scores of the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS), the scores of the Generic Quality of Life Inventory (GQOLI-74), the serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), the serum S100β protein, the neuron-specific enolase (NSE), and the Neuregulin-1 (NRG1) levels of the two groups were compared, and the adverse drug reactions of patients were recorded. After 3 months of treatment, the PANSS scores of both groups decreased compared with those before treatment, and the PANSS scores of the research group were lower. The scores of physical function, social function, and psychological function of the two groups were higher than those before treatment, and the scores of the research group were higher than those of the control group. The differences were statistically significant (p < 0.05 for all). The serum BDNF and NRG1 levels of the two groups were higher than those before treatment, and those of the research group were higher than those of the control group. The S100β and NSE levels of the two groups were lower than those before treatment, and those of the research group were lower than those of the control group. The differences were statistically significant (p < 0.05 for all). No serious adverse reactions occurred in both groups. Most patients with adverse reactions could tolerate them or improved after symptomatic treatment. Blonanserin can effectively relieve the symptoms of schizophrenia and improve the quality of life of first-episode schizophrenia patients who have failed to respond to Risperidone monotherapy in the early stage. Due to the short follow-up time and small sample size of this study, further prospective multicenter studies should be carried out in the future to observe the long-term treatment effect and provide more favorable reference for clinical practice.
keywords: S100 Calcium Binding Protein beta Subunit

title: No Silver Bullet for Rhythm Analysis.
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
abstract: A growing number of studies are quantifying rhythmic behavior in animal displays. A recent such study questioned several aspects of the commonly used methodology and proposed an alternative approach. Most notably, the choice of null hypothesis constitutes a key element of studies into rhythmic behavior. This methodological choice is particularly important because it determines the chances of finding a rhythmic behavior that is nonrandom, while also strongly influencing the interpretation of a study's conclusions. Here, we take the newly proposed approach as an opportunity to assess the current state of the art in cross-species rhythm analysis, highlighting that there exists not one single best approach. If we want to better understand rhythmic behavior and its underlying cognitive mechanisms and evolutionary origins, we need to tackle the definition of temporal randomness. Quantifying a broad variety of rhythmic behavior in different species will be essential to this endeavor, without limiting our focus to a single methodological approach.

title: Validation of the Telephone MoCA in iRBD and Parkinson's Disease with Conversion to the Standard MoCA.
abstract: Telephone-based cognitive assessment may improve follow-up when face-to-face testing is impractical. The Telephone Montreal Cognitive Assessment (T-MoCA) omits visually dependent items from the standard MoCA, but its validity in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), remains uncertain. To assess agreement between the T-MoCA and face-to-face MoCA-22 in iRBD and PD, and derive and externally validate a MoCA-22 to MoCA-30 conversion. In the Oxford Parkinson's Disease Centre (OPDC) Discovery Cohort, 137 participants (38 controls, 47 iRBD, 52 PD) completed T-MoCA and MoCA-22 assessments. Agreement was evaluated using Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, Bland-Altman analysis, and equivalence testing with ±1-point bounds. Equipercentile equating with log-linear smoothing was used to derive a MoCA-22 to MoCA-30 conversion using Discovery data (3561 tests), with validation in Tracking Parkinson's (5767 tests) and Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (5047 tests). T-MoCA and face-to-face MoCA-22 scores were statistically equivalent, with minimal bias; 83.3% of scores differed by ≤1 point. However, concordance between test formats was moderate (Lin's CCC = 0.58). Across 14,375 MoCA assessments, equipercentile equating outperformed proportional scaling in development and validation cohorts. Propagating T-MoCA-MoCA-22 variability resulted in wider prediction intervals for T-MoCA-derived MoCA-30 estimates, indicating individual-level uncertainty, with intervals estimable only for T-MoCA scores ≥17 due to sparse data. At group level, T-MoCA is a valid remote measure of non-visual MoCA domains in iRBD and PD. The equating function supports cohort-level harmonization of MoCA-22 and MoCA-30 scores, while individual T-MoCA-derived MoCA-30 estimates should be interpreted with caution.

title: Lamina Terminalis and Membrane of Liliequist Fenestration with Basal Cisternostomy: Permanent Cerebrospinal Fluid Diversion Rates in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in a Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (ShDH) remains a source of morbidity after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). During microsurgical clipping, lamina terminalis (LT) fenestration with basal cisternostomy (BC) and membrane of Liliequist (MoL) fenestration (LTF-BC) can potentially reduce shunt dependency. To evaluate permanent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) diversion rates and clinical outcomes in patients with aSAH undergoing microsurgical aneurysm occlusion with LTF-BC and MoL fenestration, and to identify factors associated with them. We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study using an institutional registry (2014-2023). Of 381 patients screened, 331 with ruptured aneurysms treated microsurgically with LTF-BC and MoL fenestration were included. Primary outcomes were permanent CSF diversion and 3-year functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS]). Multivariable logistic regression and Firth regression were performed. An external comparator analysis provided descriptive absolute risk reduction (ARR) and number needed to treat (NNT) estimates. Median age was 55 years; 56.8% were women, 81.3% had Fisher grade III-IV hemorrhage, and 39.6% had acute hydrocephalus. Temporary CSF diversion was required in 50/131 (38.2%) patients with acute hydrocephalus. At 3 years, mRS was available for 326/331 patients; 244/326 (74.8%) had a good outcome (mRS 0-3). Permanent CSF diversion was performed in 9/331 patients (2.7%). Temporary CSF diversion was the only independent predictor of 3-year shunt dependency (odds ratio (OR) 5.08, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12-23.18; P = 0.036). Independent predictors of worse 3-year functional outcome were increasing age (OR 0.96 per year, 95% CI 0.94-0.99; P = 0.003), World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grade ≥3 (OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.19-0.62; P < 0.001), and intraventricular hemorrhage (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75; P = 0.004). In external comparison, permanent CSF diversion was lower than in the nonfenestration cohort (2.7% vs 17.9%; ARR 15.2%; NNT 6.59). LTF-BC with MoL fenestration was associated with a low 3-year permanent CSF diversion rate despite high hemorrhage severity. Temporary CSF diversion identified a subgroup at increased risk for future shunt dependency.

title: Neutrophil extracellular traps drive AIM2-mediated endothelial PANoptosis and blood-brain barrier disruption after traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption is a critical pathological event contributing to secondary injury and poor outcomes following traumatic brain injury (TBI). While neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are known to exacerbate neuroinflammation, the precise molecular mechanisms by which they compromise cerebral microvascular integrity remain elusive. This study aimed to investigate the role of the NETs-AIM2 inflammasome axis in mediating endothelial damage and to explore the therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway. A controlled cortical impact (CCI) mouse model was utilized to simulate TBI. NET formation was modulated pharmacologically using the peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) inhibitor Cl-amidine or genetically via adenoviral overexpression of PAD4. BBB permeability, brain edema, and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were assessed using Evans Blue extravasation, wet-to-dry weight ratio, T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, and laser speckle contrast imaging. Neurological function was evaluated via modified Neurological Severity Score (mNSS) and rotarod tests. Molecular mechanisms were dissected using Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and cell-type-specific co-localization analyses. TBI induced significant PAD4-dependent NET formation, peaking at day 3 post-injury, which temporally coincided with BBB breakdown and neurological deficits. Cl-amidine treatment effectively preserved tight junction proteins (zonula occludens-1, Occludin) and adherens junction protein (vascular endothelial-cadherin), reduced Evans Blue extravasation, attenuated brain edema and lesion volume, promoted CBF restoration, and improved mNSS scores and rotarod performance. Mechanistically, NETs acted as upstream danger signals that specifically triggered AIM2 inflammasome activation, which was predominantly localized in cerebral microvascular endothelial cells rather than glial cells. This endothelial-specific AIM2 activation subsequently initiated PANoptosis-a multifaceted cell death program characterized by simultaneous pyroptosis, necroptosis, and apoptosis-in the vascular endothelium. Pharmacological inhibition of AIM2 effectively suppressed all three death pathways and preserved BBB integrity. Adenoviral overexpression of PAD4 exacerbated endothelial PANoptosis, whereas AIM2 inhibition reversed these effects, establishing the causal relationship. Our findings demonstrate a pathogenic axis wherein TBI-induced NETs drive endothelial PANoptosis via specific activation of the AIM2 inflammasome in cerebral microvascular endothelial cells, leading to BBB failure. Targeting this signaling cascade represents a promising therapeutic strategy to protect the neurovascular unit and improve functional recovery after TBI.

title: Spaceflight suppresses inflammasome signaling and alters dopaminergic regulation in the mouse brain from Rodent Research-1 (RR-1) mission.
abstract: Microgravity and radiation exposure during spaceflight pose significant health risks to astronauts, including disruption of physiological and neural homeostasis and increased risk of neurodegenerative disorders. Spaceflight induces neuroinflammatory responses, including inflammasome formation, which regulates innate immune signaling following cellular damage. Additionally, reduced neuromuscular activity in microgravity is associated with altered dopamine signaling. However, the direct effect on inflammasome activation and dopaminergic regulation under spaceflight is still poorly understood. In this study, we examined the genes and proteins that are associated with the inflammasome and the dopamine dysregulation associated with inflammation in mice exposed to spaceflight conditions. Mouse brains (C57BL/6J) from Rodent Research 1 (RR1, SpaceX-4) missions were analyzed based on exposure to spaceflight, simulated, and standard conditions for a baseline and control. Brain samples were analyzed for gene expression of inflammasome signaling genes and for mRNA expression to detect alterations under spaceflight conditions. Dopamine analysis was also performed to identify possible changes in major monoamines. This observation indicated that spaceflight conditions were associated with suppressed inflammasome-related gene expression with no statistically observable changes in monoamine concentration. Overall, the data established that spaceflight stressors concurrently dampen neuroinflammatory signaling while altering dopamine regulation in the brain.

title: Patient and public involvement in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis research in Japan: a survey through nationally advertised ALS Café events and a pilot advocacy training program.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) remains an incurable, progressive neurodegenerative disease. Patient and public involvement (PPI) has been increasingly recognized as a means to enhance the relevance, quality, and efficiency of research; however, its implementation in intractable neurological disease research remains limited in Japan. This webinar-based study, conducted through nationally advertised ALS Café events, aimed to clarify current PPI awareness among the Japanese ALS community and to explore strategies for promoting patient advocacy. Data were collected during the "ALS Café" held in September 2024 and a subsequent patient advocacy training program organized in October 2025. Among 79 respondents (42 patients with ALS and 37 caregivers), approximately 80% reported being unfamiliar with the concept of PPI, yet 72.2% expressed willingness to participate once the concept was explained. Among the 57 respondents willing to participate, interest was highest for involvement in translating research findings into practice (56.1%) and in identifying research themes (47.4%), and most (93%) stated that they expected no remuneration beyond reimbursement of expenses. The subsequent training program was well received, with mean evaluation scores exceeding 8.0 on a 0-10 scale, indicating high comprehensibility among participants (changes in knowledge or willingness to participate were not assessed). Respondents were a self-selected group of ALS Café participants with limited demographic characterization who may not represent patients and caregivers who do not participate in such events, and the training program evaluation lacked a pre-training baseline; these limitations should be considered when interpreting our findings. These findings reveal substantial stated willingness among Japanese patients with ALS and their caregivers to contribute to research despite low baseline awareness of PPI. This gap between limited awareness and high stated willingness suggests that targeted educational efforts could meaningfully expand patient engagement in ALS research. Systematic awareness-building initiatives, structured and accessible engagement opportunities, and sustained collaborative relationships between researchers and the patient community are essential for strengthening patient advocacy and accelerating drug development for ALS in Japan.

title: High-altitude environments elevate central and peripheral α-synuclein levels and accelerate PD-related pathology.
abstract: High-altitude exposure has been linked to an increased risk of Parkinson's disease (PD), potentially through hypoxic neuronal damage, yet the involvement of α-synuclein (α-syn) remains poorly understood. This study integrates population-based surveys, animal experiments, and clinical cross-sectional data to elucidate the role of high-altitude environments in PD pathogenesis. A cross-sectional study was conducted among middle-aged and elderly high-altitude residents. Additional cohorts (low-altitude PD patients, low-altitude controls, and high-altitude controls) were enrolled for plasma and erythrocytic α-syn measurement, and a subset of PD patients underwent transcranial sonography to assess correlations between erythrocyte indices and substantia nigra echogenicity. A53T transgenic mice were exposed to high altitude for six months and evaluated by behavioral tests, omics sequencing, α-syn assays, and immunohistochemistry. Erythrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles from PD patients were intravenously injected into wild-type mice to assess brain entry. The crude prevalence of PD tended to be higher in high-altitude populations than the national average. A53T mice exposed to high altitude displayed more severe motor deficits, elevated brain α-syn levels, and pronounced dopaminergic neuron loss. Omics analyses revealed enrichment of pathways related to IL-17, sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling, and oxidative stress in brain tissue from high-altitude versus low-altitude A53T mice, suggesting blood-brain barrier disruption and impaired α-syn clearance. In peripheral blood, both high-altitude mice and humans exhibited elevated α-syn levels compared with their low-altitude counterparts, and erythrocyte indices correlated positively with α-syn levels. After normalization to erythrocyte count and hemoglobin, however, erythrocytic α-syn did not differ between high-altitude and low-altitude controls. In mice, intravenously injected human-derived erythrocytic vesicles entered the brain. Chronic high‑altitude exposure is associated with peripheral and central α‑syn accumulation, which may be driven by a hypoxia‑induced erythrocyte pool expansion and increased α-syn burden, potentially aggravating PD‑related neuropathology.

title: The momentary associations of negative affect, anxiety and stress with symptoms in individuals with anorexia nervosa: a scoping review.
abstract: Negative affect, anxiety, and stress are common in individuals with anorexia nervosa (AN), but their momentary link to symptoms remains unclear. This review aims to (1) examine how negative affect, anxiety, and stress are associated with eating-disorder-related symptoms in the moment in individuals with AN and (2) explore how these concepts are conceptualised and measured across studies in this field. A systematic search following PRISMA-ScR guidelines was conducted across 11 databases. Eligible studies included individuals with a diagnosis of (atypical) AN, examined negative affect, anxiety, or stress, and reported outcomes related to AN symptoms. We identified 95 eligible studies, which we categorised into retrospective self-report, qualitative, experimental, and daily life studies. Across experimental paradigms, negative affect was primarily examined in relation to disorder-specific cognitions. In daily life studies, negative affect was associated with binge eating and purging, while associations with restriction and physical activity were mixed. Mealtime anxiety was related to caloric intake. Stress investigated using general stress paradigms yielded mixed findings for eating-disorder behaviours, with notable divergences between subjective and physiological stress responses. Few studies directly compared negative affect, anxiety, and stress within the same design, limiting conclusions regarding their relative importance. Negative affect, anxiety and stress are associated with disorder-specific cognitions and urges, though the translation into observable behaviour varies by context and subtype. Future research must address current gaps by adopting multi-modal assessments. Strengthening methodological consistency will be important for advancing the understanding of the interplay between affective states and symptoms in AN.

title: Smartphone and Highly Visual Social Media Use Following Acute Treatment for Anorexia Nervosa: Associations With Eating Disorder Severity and Clinical Impairment.
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
abstract: Anorexia nervosa (AN) has high relapse risk following acute treatment. Though highly visual social media (HVSM; e.g., Instagram, TikTok) use is associated with higher eating disorder (ED) psychopathology, little research has examined HVSM use during this vulnerable period. This study characterized digital engagement of women recovering from AN and investigated associations between digital engagement and ED psychopathology. Participants were N = 90 cisgender women discharged from acute AN treatment within the past 2 months, recruited for a pilot trial evaluating a digital relapse-prevention tool. Baseline surveys assessed smartphone and HVSM use, content-specific engagement, and ED psychopathology (Eating Disorder Examination-Questionnaire; Clinical Impairment Assessment). Spearman correlations and multivariable regression models were used to evaluate relationships between these variables. Instagram was the most used platform (93.3%), followed by Facebook, YouTube, Snapchat, and TikTok. Controlling for covariates, HVSM use was significantly associated with ED severity (b = 0.441, 95% CI [0.108, 0.774]) and clinical impairment (b = 3.443, 95% CI [0.602, 6.285]). Viewing and posting ED content on HVSM were each associated with greater ED severity; viewing ED content was additionally associated with clinical impairment. Engagement with ED recovery content was not associated with ED psychopathology and did not attenuate associations between HVSM use and ED psychopathology. HVSM use and ED content engagement were associated with elevated ED psychopathology in women recently discharged from AN treatment. Descriptive patterns suggest algorithmic delivery of ED content through greater reported exposure than intentional following. Clinicians may consider assessing and planning HVSM behaviors during treatment and the post-acute recovery period.

title: Disentangling global atrophy burden from local structural patterns reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity in mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a heterogeneous prodromal stage of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Imaging-based subtyping may conflate global neurodegenerative burden with local anatomical variation, limiting biological interpretability. We aimed to separate global atrophy burden from local structural patterns and assess their clinical relevance in MCI. Baseline ADNI-1 data from 731 participants were analyzed, including 205 cognitively normal individuals, 351 with MCI, and 175 with AD. A global atrophy index (GAI) was defined as the z-standardized ratio of TIV-adjusted whole-brain cerebrospinal fluid volume to TIV-adjusted gray matter plus white matter volume. Candidate regions were screened in the full CN-MCI-AD sample. Within MCI, regional measures were residualized against age, sex, education, and GAI to derive local residual structural features. Principal component analysis and unsupervised clustering were applied to identify imaging-based subtypes. Clinical associations were assessed using multivariable regression, and nested models evaluated the incremental explanatory value of continuous residual features beyond subtype labels. GAI showed a clear gradient across cognitively normal, MCI, and AD groups. After adjustment for GAI, two local residual structural patterns were identified within MCI: a thalamic-striatal lower-residual subtype and a frontal-paralimbic lower-residual subtype. Compared with the thalamic-striatal subtype, the frontal-paralimbic subtype showed greater cognitive impairment and poorer daily functioning, with higher ADAS-Cog13 and FAQ scores after covariate adjustment. Associations with neuropsychiatric symptoms were weak. Continuous PCA-derived residual features provided additional explanatory value for ADAS-Cog13 and FAQ beyond subtype labels. MCI heterogeneity is not explained solely by global atrophy. Local residual structural patterns were associated with cognitive and functional differences, and continuous residual features captured additional clinical information beyond discrete subtype labels. Separating global atrophy burden from local anatomical organization may improve interpretation of imaging heterogeneity in prodromal AD.

title: Pipelined spiking neural network equalizer architecture designed for CMOS implementation in IM/DD optical transmission systems.
abstract: High-capacity optical communication systems require nonlinear equalization with high throughput and low activity in intensity-modulation/direct-detection (IM/DD) receivers. We propose a pipelined leaky integrate, discharge, and firing (LIDF) spiking neural network (SNN) architecture designed for future CMOS implementation. LIDF separates integration from discharge and firing into two stages and combines reversed receptive field encoding with end-of-time membrane decoding. The behavioral model builds on a previously reported non-leaky two-phase circuit evaluated through SPICE simulations in the SkyWater 130 nm PDK. The synaptic-current and membrane-leakage dynamics introduced here are evaluated behaviorally on the PyTorch/Norse platform. In simulated IM/DD links, LIDF achieves gains of approximately 0.2 dB over a reference SNN equalizer, 0.7 dB over a nonlinear artificial neural network equalizer, and 1.7 dB over a linear equalizer at a pre-FEC bit-error rate of 2 · 10-3. The regularized configuration exhibits up to 91% lower spike activity under simulated conditions, indicating the potential to reduce spike-dependent dynamic energy in an event-driven implementation.

title: A Precision-Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death.
abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non-specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen (1O2) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light-controlled generation of 1O2. Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β-cells and primary islet β-cells and induces localized β-cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

title: Transdiagnostic metacognitive therapy compared to disorder-specific cognitive behavioral therapy for anxiety disorders: a study protocol for a randomized controlled superiority trial.
abstract: Anxiety disorders are highly prevalent worldwide and are associated with functional impairment, reduced quality of life and high societal costs. With only approximately 50% of patients achieving remission following cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), the evaluation of other effective treatments is warranted. Studies suggest that metacognitive therapy (MCT) may be more effective than CBT for anxiety disorders. Although transdiagnostic treatment may be beneficial for treatment implementation and dissemination in routine care, there is currently only one adequately powered study comparing transdiagnostic MCT (tMCT) to disorder-specific CBT for anxiety disorders. The main aim of this trial is to investigate the effectiveness of tMCT compared to disorder-specific CBT for anxiety disorders. The trial also aims to investigate potential mediators of treatment effects in tMCT and CBT, to conduct a health economic evaluation and to explore patients' perspectives on the treatments. This trial is a prospective, pragmatic, two-arm parallel-group randomized controlled superiority trial comparing tMCT with disorder-specific CBT, conducted in outpatient psychiatric services in Stockholm, Sweden. A sample of 86 adults with a principal diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder or posttraumatic stress disorder will be recruited and randomly allocated to tMCT or CBT. Primary outcomes are self-rated symptoms of principal diagnosis, and secondary outcomes are clinical severity, remission rates, depressive symptoms, functional impairment and quality of life. Outcomes will be assessed at pre- and post-treatment as well as at 6- and 12-month follow-up. Metacognitions and cognitions as potential mediators will be measured weekly during treatment. Cost-effectiveness of tMCT compared to CBT will be investigated. Semi-structured interviews will be conducted with participants from both conditions. Considering the potential of MCT, further research is needed to evaluate its effectiveness compared to CBT, particularly MCT in a transdiagnostic format. Results from this trial will add to the evidence base for tMCT and inform treatment development, decision-making and implementation of effective treatment for anxiety disorders in routine care. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06937892. Registered on April 22nd, 2025.

title: Escitalopram for psychological symptoms and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) often have comorbid depression and anxiety, which worsen prognosis. Escitalopram, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, is used for these symptoms, but evidence on its psychological and cardiovascular effects in CHD is limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated its effects on psychological symptoms and cardiovascular outcomes in CHD. We systematically searched five databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of escitalopram vs. control in adults with CHD. Data were extracted to avoid double counting; extended follow-up data were analyzed separately. Outcomes included depression/anxiety scale changes, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and revascularization. Random-effects models and sensitivity analyses were used. Five RCTs were included. Overall depression score change was not significant (SMD = -0.70, 95% CI -1.57 to 0.18), but medium-term (12-24 weeks) follow-up showed improvement (SMD = -0.39, 95% CI -0.58 to -0.20). Anxiety scores significantly decreased with escitalopram (SMD = -0.64, 95% CI -1.12 to -0.17). Pooled data from two studies were compatible with reductions in MACE (RR = 0.74, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.94) and myocardial infarction (RR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.96), however, approximately 90% of the pooled weight came from the post-treatment follow-up of a single trial, so these findings are hypothesis-generating. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed for all-cause mortality or revascularization. Escitalopram appears effective for selected psychological symptoms in CHD without evidence of major cardiovascular harm; current evidence is insufficient to establish a cardiovascular benefit, and the observed MACE and myocardial infarction reductions are hypothesis-generating. Treatment should aim primarily to improve psychological well-being and quality of life.

title: Correction to: Development of Cre-dependent retrograde trans-multisynaptic tracer based on pseudorabies virus bartha strain.
Differential circadian time modulates of dentate gyrus and CA1 excitation-inhibition balance and seizure threshold.
abstract: Circadian rhythms regulate seizure threshold and neuronal excitability in epilepsy. Temporal lobe seizures tend to arise more frequently during the diurnal phase relative to the nocturnal phase, yet dentate gyrus (DG) granule cells display elevated intrinsic excitability and CA1 pyramidal neurons show enhanced synaptic excitability at night. Here, we used male adult ICR mice (8-10 weeks old) as experimental subjects. Systemic pilocarpine injection was applied to pharmacologically trigger acute seizures, while AAV (pAAV2/9-CaMKIIα-hChR2 (H134R) - EYFP) delivery followed by optogenetic stimulation (10 Hz, 20 ms pulse width, 5 mW 473 nm blue light) was implemented to evoke region-specific hippocampal seizures. Combining continuous video-electroencephalography (vEEG) recording, optogenetically induced seizure assays, mRNA sequencing, and whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology, we investigated circadian modulation of neuronal excitability and seizure threshold within the DG and CA1 subfields of the hippocampus. Our results revealed divergent circadian regulation of seizure thresholds between the DG and CA1 regions. Notably, the diurnal-nocturnal seizure threshold pattern in CA1 recapitulated that seen in systemic pilocarpien-provoked seizure models. We further confirmed that circadian cycles exert distinct regulatory effects on excitatory/inhibitory synaptic transmission and the intrinsic excitability of hippocampal principal neurons in the DG and CA1. Collectively, this work highlights region-specific circadian control over seizure susceptibility and the brain excitation-inhibition balance. Elucidating circadian influences on hippocampal physiology and seizure threshold will improve the translational value of anti-epileptic therapies and guide time-stratified seizure intervention strategies.

title: Functional Network Organization Underlying Individual Differences in False Feedback Susceptibility: A Graph Theoretical Analysis.
abstract: Individual differences in susceptibility to somatosensory false physiological feedback reflect variations in interoceptive processing, yet the underlying neural network mechanisms remain unclear. We analyzed resting-state functional connectivity using graph theoretical approaches in 41 healthy adults who completed a somatosensory false feedback paradigm. Nine regions of interest were defined from previous activation analyses, and network topology metrics including local efficiency, clustering coefficient, centrality measures, and path length were calculated across multiple thresholds. Three distinct patterns of network organization predicted false feedback susceptibility. Individuals more susceptible to false feedback showed: (1) increased posterior insula eccentricity, indicating network peripheralization of this key interoceptive region; (2) consistent orbitofrontal cortex segregation across multiple metrics including increased path length and decreased centrality measures; and (3) cerebellar network reconfiguration with reduced local efficiency but increased betweenness centrality. Somatosensory false feedback susceptibility reflects specific alterations in functional network topology, particularly reduced integration of interoceptive regions (posterior insula) and emotional appraisal systems (orbitofrontal cortex). These findings support a network-based model where interoceptive processing depends on efficient integration between visceral sensation, emotional evaluation, and cognitive control systems. Understanding these network properties may inform interventions targeting interoceptive awareness and emotional regulation.

title: Neural mechanisms underlying the effects of cognitive fatigue on physical effort-based choice.
abstract: Fatigue is a state of exhaustion that influences our willingness to engage in effortful tasks. While both physical and cognitive exertion can cause fatigue, there is a limited understanding of how fatigue in one exertion domain (e.g., cognitive) affects decisions to exert in another (e.g., physical). We first trained human participants to associate their physical exertions with a numerical scale of effort levels. Participants then completed a forced-choice task for prospective physical effort before and after completing bouts of a cognitively fatiguing working memory (3-back) task. Functional magnetic resonance imaging was used to measure brain activity during the choice and 3-back tasks. Using computational modeling of choice behavior, we found that participants reported increasing levels of cognitive and physical fatigue, but it was only the increasing feelings of cognitive fatigue that made them more risk-averse for high levels of physical effort. An analysis of the functional magnetic resonance imaging findings showed that right anterior insula encodes cognitive fatigue-induced increases in participants' subjective costs of physical effort compared with a baseline rested state, while increasing activity in right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex tracked time spent on the 3-back task. A psychophysiological interaction analysis revealed that fatigue-related activations right anterior insula and right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex are correlated and that these regions are linked in an exertion-domain general fatigue network. Our results support the idea of a general fatigue signal that integrates exertion-specific information to guide effort-based choice.

title: When Athletes Ask About Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy.
abstract: Athletes exposed to repetitive head impacts (RHI) may seek clinical evaluation because of concerns about chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a neuropathologically defined disease that cannot currently be diagnosed during life. As public awareness of CTE has expanded, clinicians face challenges communicating diagnostic uncertainty, interpreting non-specific symptoms, and addressing concerns about future neurological health. This Current Opinion examines the widening gap between public expectations and scientific capability and considers its implications for athlete-centered care. We discuss how clinicians can acknowledge uncertainty without dismissing patients' concerns, identify potentially treatable contributors to symptoms without prematurely attributing them to neurodegenerative disease, and use shared decision-making to guide individualized evaluation and management. We also consider how concerns about CTE may influence decisions about continued participation and return-to-sport among current athletes. Meeting these challenges requires coordinated interdisciplinary care, evidence-based communication, and clinical approaches that prioritize meaningful intervention even when diagnostic certainty remains unavailable.

title: Remote Ischemic Post-Conditioning Modulates Brain Expression of PIWI Proteins After Experimental Cerebral Ischemia.
abstract: This study explores the involvement of PIWI family proteins in cerebral ischemia and their potential contribution to the neuroprotective effects of remote ischemic post-conditioning (RIC), a promising intervention for ischemic stroke whose underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. Using a mouse model of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAo), we evaluated the effects of RIC induced by femoral artery occlusion (FAo) on brain injury, inflammation, and PIWI proteins expression in the brain. RIC significantly reduced infarct volume, cerebral edema, and neurological deficits, while attenuating the ischemia-induced upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-1β and TNF-α, in the brain cortex. The ischemic insult induced a robust upregulation of PIWIL2 and PIWIL4 in the ipsilateral cortex, primarily in neurons, with PIWIL4 also detected in astrocytes, few microglia and numerous infiltrating myeloid cells. Notably, RIC suppressed this cortical upregulation, suggesting a potential link between PIWI proteins and ischemic damage. By contrast, in neurogenic regions of the hippocampus, RIC selectively enhanced PIWIL4 expression, particularly in neurons of the CA3 region and dentate gyrus. This increase was associated with elevated expression of the neurogenic and repair-related factors TGF-β1 and TREM2. Accordingly, in the subventricular zone of post-conditioned mice, PIWIL4 was localized in SOX2-positive neural progenitor cells that also express the proliferation marker Ki67. These findings reveal a region- and cell-specific modulation of PIWILs expression in cerebral ischemia and RIC, strongly supporting the concept that PIWI pathways may represent promising targets for neuroprotection and recovery following stroke.

title: Elevated mitochondrial metabolism in Down syndrome iPSCs reduces commitment to neuroectoderm.
abstract: A key feature of Down syndrome (DS) is reduced neurogenesis. Here, we provide evidence that increased mitochondrial metabolism in DS stem cells reduces their ability to commit to neuroectoderm (NE), one of the earliest steps in the development of the nervous system. We show that mitochondria in induced pluripotent stem cells derived from individuals with DS (3S-iPSCs) have a higher membrane potential and increased capacity for calcium uptake via the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) compared to isogenic, euploid controls. Consequently, 3S-iPSCs proliferate faster and spend less time in G1 of the cell cycle. This reduces the opportunity for growth of a primary cilium, an important developmental signaling hub. Inhibiting MCU or slowing proliferation of 3S-iPSCs is sufficient to increase ciliation and improve commitment to NE. In summary, we provide evidence that a mitochondria-to-cilia signaling axis important during the earliest steps of neurogenesis is dysregulated in DS iPSCs.

title: Spatial single-cell mapping of transcriptional differences across genetic backgrounds in mouse brains.
abstract: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. Comparative statistical analysis of organs across genetic backgrounds requires spatial, single-cell, atlas-scale data in replicates. Here we introduce atlas-scale transcriptome localization using aggregate signatures (ATLAS), a scalable tissue mapping method that learns transcriptional signatures from single-cell RNA sequencing data, encodes them in situ with tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes and decodes them to infer cell types and imputed transcriptomes. We validated ATLAS against direct MERFISH measurements of marker genes and through quantitative comparisons to four other technologies. We profiled 40 million cells across more than 400 coronal sections from central brains of five male and five female C57BL/6J mice and five male BTBR T+tf/J mice, an idiopathic autism model. Our analysis revealed more than 40 significant differences in cell-type distributions and identified 16 regional composition changes across male-female and B6-BTBR comparisons. ATLAS thus enables systematic comparative studies, facilitating organ-level structure-function analysis of disease models.

title: Selective blockade of microRNA-31-5p-calcitonin receptor interaction reverses established atrial fibrosis and atrial arrhythmia burden.
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is promoted by atrial fibrosis, a form of structural remodelling for which effective therapies are lacking. MicroRNA-31-5p (miR-31-5p), an aging-associated, atrial-enriched microRNA, has been linked to AF, but its role in atrial fibrosis is unknown. Here we show that atrial fibroblasts from patients with persistent AF exhibit increased miR-31-5p expression and reduced expression of the calcitonin receptor (CTR, encoded by CALCR). MiR-31-5p directly represses CTR and promotes pro-fibrotic fibroblast responses, whereas its inhibition restores CTR expression. Fibroblast-specific overexpression of miR-31 in mice reduces atrial CTR expression, increases atrial fibrosis and enhances arrhythmia susceptibility. Selective disruption of miR-31-5p-CALCR binding using a locked nucleic acid target site blocker restores atrial CTR expression, prevents fibrosis progression and reduces arrhythmia burden. In mice with established atrial remodeling, this strategy promotes fibrosis regression, identifying the miR-31-5p-CTR axis as a potential therapeutic target in AF.

title: Twenty years of induced pluripotent stem cells.
Electroacupuncture alleviates chronic pain and comorbid depression through Gut-Metabolite-Brain axis remodeling to restore mPFC Glu/GABA balance.
abstract: The comorbidity of chronic pain and depression is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder involving dysregulated microbiota-gut-brain communication. Although electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for both pain and depression, the mechanisms linking peripheral microbial-metabolic remodeling to central neurotransmitter regulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach in a spared nerve injury (SNI) rat model to investigate the gut-metabolite-brain mechanisms underlying EA's efficacy. EA significantly alleviated mechanical hypersensitivity and depressive-like behaviors while restoring mPFC Glu/GABA balance, accompanied by normalization of the glutamate transporter EAAT2 and the GABA-synthesizing enzyme GAD67. Metagenomic analysis showed that EA remodeled the gut microbial ecosystem by increasing microbial diversity, suppressing opportunistic pathobionts, including Bacillus cereus, Alistipes onderdonkii, while enriching SCFA-associated genera, including Butyricimonas and Romboutsia. These alterations were accompanied by coordinated remodeling of amino acid and butanoate metabolism. Correlation network analysis identified Pipecolic acid as a central metabolic node linking gut microbial alterations with mPFC GABAergic neurotransmission and behavioral recovery. Although individual bacterial genera did not significantly mediate its restoration, causal mediation analysis demonstrated that the Pipecolic acid-GABA axis significantly mediated improvements in both mechanical allodynia and anhedonia, supporting Pipecolic acid as a functional metabolic hub linking peripheral metabolic remodeling to central GABAergic regulation. Collectively, these findings identify peripheral metabolic remodeling as a key mechanistic interface through which EA coordinates gut microbial ecology and central neurochemical homeostasis, providing a systems-level framework for understanding the therapeutic mechanisms of acupuncture in pain-depression comorbidity.

title: Genotype and phenotype analyses of 689 individuals with PCDH19-clustering epilepsy.
abstract: PCDH19-clustering epilepsy (PCDH19-CE) is an infantile-onset neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by clusters of seizures, typically triggered by fever. PCDH19-CE follows an unusual X-linked inheritance pattern whereby heterozygous females, and males with X-chromosome disomy or pathogenic postzygotic mosaic PCDH19 variants, are affected, while hemizygous males are spared.
