We aggregate published PCDH19 variants and their corresponding PCDH19-CE phenotypes to analyse phenotype-genotype correlations. Data extracted from 110 publications identified 689/735 (94%) individuals with PCDH19 variants and the typical PCDH19-CE phenotype. Three hundred seventy-three unique PCDH19 variants were identified; 195 were not recorded in ClinVar. Seizure onset prior to 12 months of age was associated with more severe intellectual disability (p < 0.001) and the presence of psychiatric morbidity (p = 0.001). There were no phenotypic differences between missense, nonsense, and frameshift variants or between individuals of different geographical backgrounds, which was assessed as a proxy for ancestry. Twenty-nine hemizygous males with constitutive PCDH19 variants did not exhibit the typical PCDH19-CE phenotype, suggesting that the identification of variants in these individuals likely results from chance or ascertainment bias. The correlation between earlier seizure onset and poorer neurodevelopmental outcomes emphasises a critical window for therapeutic intervention. The lack of phenotypic difference between variant types demonstrates that loss of PCDH19 function underpins PCDH19-CE. Moreover, the identification of PCDH19 cytoplasmic domain variants in 78 affected individuals challenges the traditional view that PCDH19-CE is caused primarily by defects in cell-cell adhesion, as variants in this domain are expected to disrupt the nuclear function(s) of PCDH19.

title: Identification of fluid endocannabinoid and sphingolipid biomarkers in schizophrenia. A machine learning approach toward clinical value.
abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) diagnosis relies on subjective clinical evaluation, with symptoms often overlapping between psychiatric conditions, hindering early intervention, and creating an urgent need for objective, accessible biomarkers. Lipids, especially endocannabinoid system (ECS) and sphingolipid metabolism members, are promising candidates given their implication in SCZ pathogenesis and measurability in accessible biofluids, with minimally invasive procedures. Our study conducted the first comprehensive crossover of endocannabinoids (eCBs) and sphingolipids in matched cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum samples from antipsychotic-naïve SCZ patients (SCZnaïve, n = 49), antipsychotic-treated patients (SCZtreat, n = 56), and healthy volunteers (HVs, n = 51). The machine learning Integrated Disease Explanation and Risk Scoring (IDEARS) platform was applied to eCBs, N-acylethanolamines, ceramides, and sphingomyelins quantified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, identifying key discriminatory features across biofluids and conditions (CSF AUC: SCZnaïve = 0.87, SCZtreat = 0.94; serum AUC: SCZnaïve = 0.87, SCZtreat = 0.90). Anandamide emerged as the top CSF feature in SCZnaïve patients, showing significantly elevated levels (q = 0.010) compared to HVs. Notably, though not statistically significant under conventional statistics, IDEARS identified anandamide as a top ten serum feature. Additionally, elevated sphingadiene backbone (d18:2) sphingolipids were conserved between the CSF and serum of SCZnaïve (q C24) species potentially reflecting antipsychotic metabolic effects. Our results support the involvement of the ECS and sphingolipid imbalances in SCZ, highlighting the potential of machine learning for novel biomarker discovery, including stratification across biofluids, and therapeutic monitoring toward more objective psychiatric care.

title: Mitochondrial complex IV disruption is a detrimental pathology conferring ssusceptibility to alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) is an integral part of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) and plays a pivotal role in maintaining mitochondrial function. In contrast to the long-standing recognition of its dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the exact role of CIV deficit in the pathogenesis of this neurodegenerative disorder remains poorly defined. In this study, by incorporating clinical resources, mouse- and human-based models of AD risk, and a genetic approach to bypass defective CIV via the ectopic expression of alternative oxidase (AOX), we examined whether CIV deficits are a pathogenic driver of or a beneficial adaptation to AD-associated pathologies. Our results showed a clinicopathological association between neuronal CIV dysfunction and pathological characteristics of AD. Further experiments linked defective CIV to the development of mitochondrial dysfunction and synaptic loss in the tested mouse- and human-based models of AD risk. In addition, a reciprocal relationship between CIV dysfunction and amyloid pathology was determined. Lastly, a proteome-wide association study (PWAS) using genetic data from large-scale AD cohorts identified that downregulation of COX11, a crucial CIV assembly factor, confers susceptibility to AD risk. Collectively, our findings suggest that CIV dysfunction is a detrimental pathology contributing to AD-associated mitochondrial and neuronal damage. The dual role of CIV dysfunction, both as a consequence of and a contributor to amyloid toxicity in AD pathogenesis, further justifies the therapeutic potential of strategies targeting CIV deficits to diversify the tools for prevention and treatment of this neurodegenerative disorder.

title: Implementation strategies for digital relapse prevention in schizophrenia identified during a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Digital mental health technologies hold promise, yet their integration into routine care remains challenging. This study reports findings from an implementation workshop conducted midway through an ongoing multi-site randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating a smartphone-based relapse prevention app for patients with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder. Sixteen stakeholders, including developers, researchers, and clinicians, discussed experiences and barriers using a semi-structured agenda, incorporating prior feedback from three focus groups with people with lived experience, and analyzed the discussions using an adopted R(E)-AIM framework (Reach, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance). Findings highlight the need for structural, technical, and personnel adjustments to support sustainable implementation. Key recommendations include integrating digital tools into discharge planning, enhancing interdisciplinary collaboration, delegating digital responsibilities, and streamlining technical workflows to facilitate seamless adoption. These insights inform feasibility considerations and strategic requirements for digital interventions in severe mental illness, offering guidance for future RCTs and practice-oriented integration of digital therapeutics in psychiatric care.

title: Tau positron emission tomography harmonization using the CenTauR approach: General conversion equations, relevant cut-points, and external validation.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Tau positron emission tomography (PET) tracers differ in kinetics, binding properties, and quantification pipelines, complicating cross-study comparisons. The CenTauR approach provides a unified framework for harmonizing tau PET quantification across tracers. We defined a tracer-agnostic "Standard Method" using Statistical Parametric Mapping 12, standardized regions of interest, and harmonized acquisition parameters. Using data from five tau tracers-[18F]flortaucipir, [18F]MK-6240, [18F]PI-2620, [18F]RO948, and [18F]GTP1-we applied the Joint Propagation Model to derive linear equations converting regional standardized uptake value ratios into the tracer-independent CenTauR scale. Validation included independent cross-sectional, longitudinal, and test-retest datasets across multiple cohorts. The CenTauR scale yielded highly consistent regional values across tracers, with strong cross-tracer agreement and robust performance in external validation cohorts. We also expressed clinically relevant cut-points and staging boundaries on the CenTauR scale. The CenTauR approach enables harmonized, tracer-independent quantification of tau PET, supporting reproducibility across studies and improving interpretation in clinical research and multicenter trials.

title: Retinal microvasculature alterations are associated with mild behavioral impairment in Southeast Asian dementia-free older adults.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Mild behavioral impairment (MBI) is an important neurobehavioral marker of dementia. This study examined associations between retinal vascular measures, MBI, and its potential neurobiological correlates. Dementia-free older adults from a memory clinic cohort were followed for up to 5 years. MBI was evaluated using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory. Retinal vessel caliber measures were quantified from fundus photographs. Associations of retinal vascular measures with neuroimaging markers of cerebral small vessel disease and plasma proteomic profiles were further explored. Among 302 participants, reduced arteriole-to-venule ratio (AVR) and narrower arteriole caliber (central retinal artery equivalent) were associated with a greater likelihood of incident MBI. Lower AVR was associated with white matter hyperintensity volume and circulating proteins related to immune function and inflammatory processes. Retinal microvascular alterations are associated with MBI in the pre-dementia stage, with exploratory findings suggesting related vascular and inflammatory biological correlates that warrant further investigation.

title: Integrative Evolutionary and Structural Analysis of GBA1 Provides Insights Into Mutation-Specific Effects Associated With Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: GBA1 encodes lysosomal acid β-glucosidase (glucocerebrosidase [GCase]), a key lysosomal enzyme and one of the most important genetic factors in Parkinson's disease (PD). Yet how different GBA1 variants influence PD-related molecular pathology remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated phylogenetic, comparative sequence, structural, docking, and molecular dynamics analyses to identify evolutionarily constrained features of GBA1 that may influence its interaction with α-synuclein (SNCA) and thereby contribute to PD pathogenesis. Phylogenetic reconstruction indicated that GBA1 originated early in bilaterian evolution and was maintained as a single-copy gene in the sampled taxa, consistent with strong functional constraint. Sequence-based analyses across sarcopterygian lineages further supported pervasive purifying selection, especially within the TIM barrel catalytic domain. Comparative structural analyses highlighted a conformationally sensitive segment spanning Residues 379-389, which includes catalytic and neighboring residues and showed recurrent involvement in both mammalian evolution and PD-associated mutant proteins. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations of wild-type and mutant GBA1-SNCA complexes indicated that PD-associated substitutions can remodel hydrogen-bond networks and influence the conformational landscape of the GBA1-SNCA complex in a mutation-specific manner. Although no statistically significant differences in global structural or energetic properties were detected, individual variants exhibited distinct patterns of conformational deviation, flexibility, and interaction dynamics relative to wild type. In particular, Residues 387-389 emerged as part of a structurally responsive region linked to altered GBA1-SNCA association. Together, these findings highlight candidate structural determinants for future experimental studies of GBA1-associated neurodegeneration.

title: Practical considerations for the implementation of daxibotulinumtoxinA for injection for management of cervical dystonia.
abstract: DaxibotulinumtoxinA (DAXI) for injection is approved for treatment of adults with cervical dystonia (CD) and is the first botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) to be formulated with a novel, custom-engineered peptide. To provide practical considerations for incorporating DAXI into clinical practice based on real-world experience from early adopters. The perspectives and practical considerations were informed by a panel of physicians with extensive experience treating CD with BoNT who participated in a DAXI early-experience program. Considerations were drafted based on individual physician questionnaire responses and finalized through individual and group discussions. All authors reviewed and approved the final practical considerations. Patients experiencing symptom re-emergence before retreatment with their current BoNT or seeking longer-lasting symptom relief are the primary candidates for DAXI. For patients switching from other BoNTs, the initial DAXI dose can be proportional to their prior onabotulinumtoxinA-equivalent dose, recognizing that units of different BoNTs are not interchangeable, with titration to an appropriate maintenance dose over 2-3 cycles. The low rate of dysphagia and muscle weakness adverse events provides a foundation for safe implementation and dose titration. Early real-world experience suggests that DAXI can be readily implemented in practice. Optimal individual dosing is established in 2-3 treatments, and retreatments can be timed to address symptom re-emergence. Consistent with phase 3 clinical trials, DAXI demonstrates a long duration of action and wide safety margin, offering long-lasting symptom relief and potentially greater flexibility in patients who experience early symptom re-emergence within a standard 12-week retreatment interval.

title: The 2025-2030 dietary guidelines for Americans through the lens of diabetes: what the Mediterranean diet can teach. Perspective from the nutrition and diabetes study group of Italian diabetes societies AMD-SID and the Italian society of dietetics and clinical nutrition (ADI).
journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
abstract: To examine the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines for Americans (DGA) against current scientific evidence and compare them with the most recent evidence-based dietary recommendations for diabetes prevention and management. The updated DGA appropriately emphasize reducing ultra-processed foods and added sugars while encouraging the consumption of whole foods. However, several recommendations warrant careful consideration in the context of diabetes prevention and management. The proposed increase in protein intake and the limited distinction between animal and plant protein sources are not supported by current evidence, which favors an individualized approach to protein intake and prioritizes protein quality over quantity. Likewise, the emphasis on whole-fat dairy products, butter, and beef tallow appears inconsistent with recommendations to limit saturated fat intake and may generate uncertainty in individuals at high cardiometabolic risk. Conversely, substantial evidence supports dietary patterns that emphasize overall dietary quality rather than macronutrient composition, with the Mediterranean Diet (MD) providing the strongest evidence for improving glycemic control and long-term cardiometabolic health. Furthermore, the updated DGA largely overlook the environmental sustainability of dietary recommendations, whereas the MD is consistently associated with a lower environmental impact than more animal-based models. Several recommendations included in the 2025-2030 DGA appear insufficiently supported by current evidence for diabetes prevention and management. Future dietary guidelines may benefit from a more integrated approach that better reflects the interplay between diet, human health, and environmental sustainability, with the MD representing the most robust evidence-based reference model.
